solution: Let A=HHTHT and B=THHHT. Track the longest suffix of the tosses so far that is also a proper prefix of either pattern. The relevant states are ∅, H, HH, HHT, HHTH, T, TH, THH, THHH. Let w(s) be the probability A wins from state s. The fair-coin recurrences, with w(A)=1 and w(B)=0, give: w(HHTH)=1/2; w(HHT)=(w(HHTH)+w(THH))/2; w(HH)=(w(HHT)+w(THH))/2; w(H)=(w(HH)+w(TH))/2; w(THHH)=w(HHT)/2; w(THH)=(w(THHH)+w(HHT))/2; w(TH)=(w(THH)+w(H))/2; w(T)=(w(TH)+w(H))/2; and w(∅)=(w(H)+w(T))/2. Solving yields w(∅)=7/12.
insight: The state after a toss is determined by the longest suffix that is a prefix of either target pattern.
insight_justification: Any earlier tosses outside that suffix cannot help complete a target pattern, so these suffix states retain all information needed to compute the next-step transition and eventual winner.
